question: Which content-policy category model should ClawHub adopt, and which consequences should each category have for visibility, review, installability, and account enforcement?
rationale: Current main has partial policy and scanner guidance, but choosing category boundaries and public-versus-reviewer-only wording is a maintainer/security policy decision, not a safe automated source change.

options.title: Synthesize And Accept A Matrix
options.body: Post a maintainer synthesis comment and land docs/spec updates that separate public policy, trust signals, scanner interpretation, and account consequences.

options.title: Narrow To Scanner Semantics First
options.body: Resolve the VirusTotal, ClawScan, SkillSpector, and Review/Malicious semantics now while deferring crypto and positive trust-signal buckets to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Supersede With Focused RFCs
options.body: Close this only after opening or linking clearer RFCs for the remaining category boundaries so the existing discussion is not lost.

recommendation.title: Synthesize And Accept A Matrix
recommendation.body: Post a maintainer synthesis comment and land docs/spec updates that separate public policy, trust signals, scanner interpretation, and account consequences.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick authored the RFC and has the strongest current docs/scanner ownership signal for this policy area.
